assets.name: Linguacore
assets.tagline: Language proficiency your teams can be measured on.
assets.mission: Give every global team a shared, verifiable standard of professional language fluency.
assets.vision: A future where language is never the reason a deal, a hire, or a rollout stalls.
assets.values: Rigor over rah-rah. Every claim is backed by an assessment score. Fluency is a business metric, not a soft skill. We report progress the way finance reports revenue: on a schedule, in writing, without spin.
assets.about: We were built inside an HR department that was tired of paying for language training it could not measure. Three years later we are the system of record forty enterprise L&D teams use to certify that their people can actually operate in the language they were hired to use.
assets.founder_story: Our founders ran global mobility for a Fortune 500 company and watched three expensive relocations fail because 'conversational fluency' on a resume meant nothing under pressure. They built the assessment first and the course content second, which is backwards for this industry and, they'd argue, the entire point.
homepage: Certify fluency. Don't guess at it.
The language assessment your compliance team will actually accept.
Every learner gets a score. Every score is defensible in a promotion review.
product_page: A four-skill assessment (reading, writing, listening, spoken) benchmarked against the CEFR scale, re-scored quarterly.
Course content is assigned only where the assessment shows a gap — no generic curriculum, no wasted seat time.
Manager dashboards report fluency the way they already report headcount: by team, by quarter, by risk.
cta: Book a benchmark assessment for your team.
See the scorecard before you buy the course.
Talk to L&D procurement, not sales.
blog: We audited 4,000 self-reported 'fluent' resumes against our assessment. Sixty-one percent scored below working proficiency. Here is what that costs a relocation program.
Why we refuse to issue a certificate without a proctored assessment behind it, even when clients ask us to skip it for a faster launch.
CEFR B2 is not a vibe. It is six specific things a speaker can do under pressure. We list all six.
social: A fluency claim without a score attached is a hope, not a hire criterion.
We turned down a logo customer this quarter because they wanted the certificate without the assessment. Still turning them down.
ad: Stop promoting on self-reported fluency. Start promoting on a score.
Your next relocation failure is probably a language gap nobody measured. Measure it first.
job_post: We need someone who gets uncomfortable when a metric can't be traced back to a raw assessment score. If dashboards without an audit trail bother you, apply.
You will say no to feature requests that make the numbers look better without making the fluency better. That is the job.
support_doc: Assessment scores are locked once submitted and cannot be edited by an administrator, including us — this is what makes the certificate defensible.
Re-assessment windows open automatically at 90 days; there is no manual override to shorten this.
case_study: A logistics firm relocating 200 engineers used our benchmark to cut failed placements from 1 in 4 to 1 in 20 over eighteen months, with the assessment data submitted directly to their immigration counsel.
testimonial: Our old vendor sent us a certificate. Linguacore sent us a score, the raw transcript, and a re-test date. That is the difference between a training vendor and a system of record.
